Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: native pixel crop motion sprite atlas for a browser farming game
Input images: Image 1 is the reference for the mature ambermelon crop identity, silhouette, palette relationships, and grounded root.
Primary request: create one transparent 4 by 4 sprite atlas for the mature ambermelon crop. Put exactly ten separate panels in the first ten cells in reading order: four idle panels in the top row, then six action panels in the second row. Leave the remaining six cells fully transparent. Each panel contains the same single an ambermelon vine with orange-gold round fruits, broad green leaves, and curling runners, centered over the same ground pivot, with broad clean pixel clusters and readable geometry.
Style/medium: crisp hand-authored 24-color pixel art, one-pixel hard edges, selective dark outline, light from upper left, shadow lower right, native game sprite.
Composition/framing: each panel is an isolated crop on a transparent background, no soil tile, no grid lines, no border; every crop root/base stays on one consistent ground line.
Lighting/mood: calm idle motion, then a readable harvest-ready rustle.
Color palette: use only the 24-color sprite palette visible in the reference and preserve the reference crop's distinctive colors.
Materials/textures: broad flat clusters, 2-3 value ramps per material, no grain or noise.
Motion plan: idle leaves and fruit highlights shift in clusters; action gathers the runners, peaks with one fruit and leaf fan lifting, then settles with the fruit grounded. All ten poses must change internal leaves, stems, petals, fruit or silhouette shape; do not create rigid whole-image translations.
Constraints: preserve mature ambermelon identity from the reference; make all ten poses visibly authored with changed internal shapes; preserve transparent alpha; no image text; no labels; no watermark; no duplicated mirrored panels.
Avoid: photorealism, soft gradients, anti-aliased edges, speckle noise, tiny decorative pixels, extra plants, soil, tools, text, numbers, shadows outside the crop, or moving the entire crop as a rigid block.
